verdict.rationale: Foreloop turns its own user-feedback submissions into intentions with agent-proposed tasks. Once a person approves them, a local Claude Code or Codex agent claims those tasks and opens a PR. This is a ticket-to-agent flow, but it starts only from Foreloop's internal reports, and agents pull approved work rather than being directly assigned it. missing for 10: integration with existing issue trackers (GitHub Issues, Jira, Linear), direct assignment of a specific ticket to a specific agent, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can assign a coding task to an agent directly from an existing issue or ticket

citations.quote: An intention starts from the report, and its agent reads the submission, fills in the intention, and proposes the tasks
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
Nothing runs until a person approves a contract.
